d: While seeking to meet film star Troy Donahue, Laverne and Shirley are mistaken for stuntwomen and get involved in some wild scenes.
Exidor's long-lost mother arrives to stop her son's marriage.
Mork is overjoyed when Fred returns and announces that he's remarried, but for Mindy, it dredges up painful memories of her mother's death.
Mork haplessly gets involved with a group of white supremacists.
Mindy takes a job writing the Miss Lonely Hearts newspaper column and unknowingly encourages Jean to pursue a romantic relationship with Mork.
Mork decides to become a priest.
Over the protests of Richie, whose parents are out of town, Potsie invites three-stranded beauty pageant contestants to spend the night.

Richie is sick in bed with the flu and is bored with eating soup and doing crossword puzzles. But when his family leaves him alone in the house, pandemonium breaks loose when Fonzie, Potsie, Ralph, and a burglar join him.
Richie, Potsie, and Ralph Malph visit another part of town to meet some girls and find themselves in trouble when the girls' boyfriends show up. Fonzie steps in to save the day.
It's a new experience for Richie when he becomes romantically attracted to an "older woman."
Richie lets fame go to his head when he takes a turn as a disc jockey at the local radio station.

st: Murder On The Moose Jaw Express (Part 1)
d: While on a train to Canada, Laverne and Shirley encounter a dying man who gives them a top-secret film and a mysterious clue to the identity of his murderer.

st: Murder On The Moose Jaw Express (Part 2)
d: Laverne and Shirley concoct a scheme to come face-to-face with the killer who has tried to poison Shirley and who has kidnapped Lenny and Squiggy.
Sgt. Alvinia Plout, the girls’ Women’s Army Corps’ nemesis, talks them into participating in an army survival test.
Laverne and Shirley lose their jobs and move to California to realize their dreams of fame and romance.

While in Chicago with their high school choir, Richie, Ralph, and Potsie sneak by their chaperons, wind up on the wrong side of an unsympathetic downtown nightclub owner, and win the sympathy of a kind-hearted cocktail waitress.

To raise money for the big football game, the boys decide to start their own babysitting service. In Football Frolics, Richie, Potsie, and Ralph have their hopes set on seeing the big football game of the year, but tickets can't be found anywhere.

When Fonzie sets a pigeon coop atop the Cunningham garage and the roof caves, Mr. Cunningham sues to collect damages. In Two Angry Men, Laverne and Shirley prevail upon Fonzie to care for a coop of pigeons.
After reading too many foreign car manuals, Fonzie is plagued with headaches and is forced to wear glasses for a few weeks, but fears glasses aren't cool.
The Malachi brothers sabotage Pinky's car the night before the demolition derby.
Shirley discovers that the wife of the about-to-be-divorced man she loves, is her mirror image.
Lenny and Squiggy have Edna talking to herself when they tell her that they’ve developed a radical new style of movies—silent films.
Laverne and Shirley unknowingly eat cookies laced with marijuana at a party and soon find themselves on the verge of marrying two British rock stars.
Laverne and Shirley hilariously try to cover their tracks after entering their supervisor’s office to retrieve a nasty note they’ve written to him.
Squiggy forgets his lines in a play written by Shirley, so Laverne and Shirley cover all the parts while a famed Broadway producer watches from the audience.
Mork becomes so hopelessly addicted to advertisements that they invade his dreams.
Fred confesses that he's having marital difficulties, so Mork and Mindy relay stories of their troubled times.
